A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MTAVG-Bench. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, including image-based figures, and retained methods, tables, prompts, and cases can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 12 omni-models, input ablations, and human assessments of generated videos in Tables 3–5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and reports additional generator-specific evaluations, automatic quality assessments, and annotation-agreement estimates in Tables 6–8.

M1.justification: The core failure-mining and diagnostic-QA pipeline, four-level/nine-dimension framework, question formats, and original inference prompts remain unchanged. Expanded annotation descriptions document the existing procedure; the new automatic quality assessment is a supplementary evaluation.

E1.justification: The diagnostic benchmark and multitalker generation tasks remain the same, including evaluation of unfiltered outputs already present in v1. EmpatheticDialogues is newly identified as the prompt source, without evidence of a dataset replacement. Additional generators are evaluated within the retained task.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds LTX 2.3 and Ovi to the human comparison previously containing Sora2, VEO 3.1, and WAN 2.5. The 12-model evaluator roster in Table 3 is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 introduces evaluation on generator-specific subsets and an automatic assessment of unfiltered outputs using AudioBox Aesthetics, ImageBind cosine similarities, and six dimension-specific Gemini 3 Pro ratings on a 1–5 scale. The original diagnostic scoring equations remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that the main benchmark was rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses examine generator dependence of evaluator rankings (Table 6) and automatically assess failures under natural output distributions (Table 7). Figures 18–25 add eight annotated failure examples. The original audio/prompt ablation and evaluator case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix D and Table 8 newly report pre-adjudication Krippendorff's alpha for nine dimensions, ranging from 0.65 to 0.88, alongside independently repeated annotation. v1 reports no agreement estimates. This does not establish additional model runs or introduce performance confidence intervals.

E6.justification: v2 adds Tables 6–8 and LTX 2.3/Ovi results averaging 43%/33% in Table 5. Retained VEO 3.1 speech-quality and camera-alignment values change from 91%/41% to 90%/40%. Figure 2's dimension counts now total 2,669 instead of 2,410, without explaining their relationship to Table 1's unchanged 2,410 QAs. Tables 3–4 retain all numerical values.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(3), defining question scores, dimension averages, and the overall average, are unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical results or proofs; the new empirical scoring rubrics do not introduce formal mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion make the existing diagnostic purpose more explicit, emphasizing omni-model failure identification and distinguishing evaluator limitations from generator weaknesses. The headline 'first comprehensive benchmark' framing is softened, while the four-level contribution and Gemini 3 Pro overall-performance claim remain.

C2.justification: New Sections 5.2–5.3 interpret failures as recurring under natural generation distributions and evaluator rankings as robust across generators. Appendix G adds the substantive qualification that inflated MLLM ratings support relative comparisons rather than absolute quality estimates. The benchmark-results discussion also tempers v1's stronger claims of uniquely reliable evaluation.

D1.justification: v2 identifies EmpatheticDialogues and 32 dialogue themes, documents three independent annotators per sample from a 21-person pool, Label Studio, expert adjudication, and additional review. It adds a benchmark access link, detailed failure descriptions, automatic-evaluation tools, and six judge prompts. However, the new Table 11 reverses SA/TT groupings relative to Table 2 and Figure 2.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to LTX-2, MOVA, ImageBind, and EmpatheticDialogues, with a limited refinement toward diagnostic positioning. The existing related-work comparisons largely remain. The JavisGPT bibliographic update and JarvisBench-to-JavisBench spelling correction do not introduce different works.

P1.justification: The title, author header, abstract, contributions, results discussion, and conclusion receive targeted revisions. Analysis and appendix subsections, an ethics statement, and acknowledgments are added, while the main section sequence and much of the original prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds seven tables, six prompt figures, and eight failure visualizations, and groups Table 5 into commercial and open-source models. Figure 2 is redesigned and relocated, removing its stacked-bar panel. Original case-study figures and the question-type distribution chart are retained under new numbers.

improvement.justification: The disclosed data source, annotation protocol, agreement estimates, and generator-specific checks improve reproducibility and credibility beyond v1's sparse documentation. These gains are limited by unexplained Figure 2 counts and contradictory SA/TT labels in Table 11. Also, despite Appendix G's useful warning about inflated judge scores, Table 7's near-ceiling structural ratings do not clearly substantiate the claimed structural-quality gap. The net quality gain is modest.
